lessons.title: Gladbach · the rise of the Foals
lessons.subtitle: Borussia joined Germany’s new national league in the mid-1960s and quickly became a title contender.

story.title: A new top flight
story.body: Borussia entered the Bundesliga in 1965, alongside Bayern Munich. The club guide traces the long run of first-division seasons that followed.

story.title: A standard of its own
story.body: The guide records Gladbach’s players and milestones as of its 2023 publication, giving a dated snapshot of the club’s scale in the league.

facts.label: Bundesliga entry
facts.prompt: In which year did Borussia Mönchengladbach first compete in the Bundesliga?
facts.evidence: The official guide gives the club’s Bundesliga seasons as 1965–99, establishing 1965 as the first season.

facts.label: Bundesliga seasons by 2023
facts.prompt: How many Bundesliga seasons had Borussia Mönchengladbach played by the historical guide’s 2023 snapshot?
facts.scope: Bundesliga appearance count in the guide published 10 July 2023.
facts.evidence: The guide explicitly lists 57 seasons in the Bundesliga, covering 1965–99, 2001–07 and 2008 onward at publication. The historical guide reports 57 Bundesliga seasons at its 2023 publication date.

facts.label: Club appearance record
facts.prompt: Which player held Borussia Mönchengladbach’s Bundesliga appearance record in the 2023 historical guide?
facts.scope: Gladbach Bundesliga records as listed in the 2023 historical guide.
facts.evidence: The guide names Berti Vogts as the appearances leader with 419.

lessons.title: Gladbach · twelve goals on the final day
lessons.subtitle: The 1977/78 finale produced a record score, but it did not bring the title back to Gladbach.

story.title: Chasing the table
story.body: On 29 April 1978, Borussia needed to overhaul Cologne’s goal-difference advantage. They attacked relentlessly against Dortmund.

story.title: A record without the prize
story.body: Gladbach scored twelve, yet Cologne’s simultaneous 5–0 win still left the Foals three goals short on goal difference.

facts.label: Record-win date
facts.prompt: On what date did Borussia Mönchengladbach beat Borussia Dortmund 12–0 in the Bundesliga?
facts.scope: Bundesliga match on the final day of 1977/78.
facts.evidence: The Bundesliga account dates the match to 29 April 1978. The official league history identifies 29 April 1978 as the day of the 12–0 result.

facts.label: Five-goal scorer
facts.prompt: Which Borussia Mönchengladbach forward scored five times against Borussia Dortmund in the 12–0 Bundesliga win?
facts.evidence: The league guide records Heynckes as the five-goal scorer. The historical guide states Heynckes scored five in the 12–0 win.

facts.label: Title-race margin
facts.prompt: By how many goals did 1. FC Köln finish ahead of Borussia Mönchengladbach on goal difference after the 1977/78 Bundesliga final day?
facts.scope: Final table of the 1977/78 Bundesliga season.
facts.evidence: Cologne’s 5–0 victory left it three goals better off than Gladbach. The league account says Cologne claimed the title by three goals after the simultaneous wins.

lessons.title: Gladbach · the 1977 European Cup final
lessons.subtitle: Borussia reached the European Cup final in Rome, where Liverpool’s late penalty settled a 3–1 match.

story.title: Road to Rome
story.body: Gladbach’s 1976/77 European Cup run ended at the Stadio Olimpico against Liverpool, after Allan Simonsen briefly brought the teams level.

story.title: A final decided late
story.body: Terry McDermott and Tommy Smith scored before Phil Neal’s penalty. The result gave Liverpool its first European Champion Clubs’ Cup.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Gladbach face Liverpool in the 1977 European Cup final?
facts.evidence: The Bundesliga guide records Gladbach’s 1977 final appearance; UEFA dates the final 25 May 1977. UEFA’s match account dates the Liverpool–Gladbach final to Wednesday, 25 May 1977.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score when Borussia Mönchengladbach faced Liverpool in the 1977 European Cup final?
facts.evidence: The Bundesliga guide says Gladbach lost the final to Liverpool; UEFA gives the result as 3–1. UEFA lists Liverpool 3–1 Borussia Mönchengladbach.

facts.label: Final venue
facts.prompt: In which city was the final played?
facts.evidence: UEFA identifies the venue as the Stadio Olimpico in Rome. UEFA lists the Stadio Olimpico, Rome as the final venue.

lessons.title: Günter Netzer · a decade in Gladbach
lessons.subtitle: Netzer’s Gladbach years made him one of the central playmakers of the club’s rise.

story.title: A long home spell
story.body: Netzer joined Borussia as a teenager in 1963 and remained through June 1973. The DFB profile counts 269 appearances for the club.

story.title: From Gladbach to Madrid
story.body: His last Gladbach match was the 1973 cup final; after the season, he moved to Real Madrid. His Germany career brought 37 senior caps.

facts.label: Borussia spell
facts.prompt: From which year did Günter Netzer’s Borussia Mönchengladbach club spell begin?
facts.evidence: The DFB Datencenter lists his Borussia dates as 1 July 1963 through 30 June 1973. The DFB profile gives the club spell beginning 1 July 1963.

facts.label: Borussia appearances
facts.prompt: How many total appearances does the DFB profile list for Günter Netzer at Borussia Mönchengladbach?
facts.scope: All listed German-club appearances for Borussia Mönchengladbach.
facts.evidence: The DFB profile lists 269 appearances for Borussia; 230 of these were Bundesliga matches. DFB’s club-history table gives Netzer 269 Borussia matches across competitions.

facts.label: Next club
facts.prompt: Which club did Günter Netzer join after leaving Borussia Mönchengladbach in 1973?
facts.scope: Netzer’s move after the end of his Gladbach career in 1973.
facts.evidence: UEFA’s Netzer profile says he negotiated a move to Real Madrid in early 1973. UEFA identifies Real Madrid as his next club.

lessons.title: Günter Netzer · the cup-final goal
lessons.subtitle: Netzer entered the 1973 DFB Cup final late and scored the extra-time winner against Cologne.

story.title: A substitute’s final
story.body: Coach Hennes Weisweiler initially left Netzer on the bench for his last Gladbach match. When Christian Kulik was injured in extra time, Netzer stepped onto the pitch.

story.title: Two touches later
story.body: Netzer struck the winner, turning the final into one of the most remembered episodes in German cup history.

facts.label: Cup-final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Günter Netzer’s Borussia Mönchengladbach beat 1. FC Köln in the 1973 DFB Cup final?
facts.evidence: The DFB Datencenter lists the final on 23 June 1973. The official DFB match record gives the final date as Saturday, 23 June 1973.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Günter Netzer’s Borussia Mönchengladbach defeat in the 1973 DFB Cup final?
facts.evidence: The DFB match record lists 1. FC Köln as the opponent. DFB’s final match record names 1. FC Köln.

facts.label: Final result
facts.prompt: What was the final score after extra time in the 1973 DFB Cup final between Borussia Mönchengladbach and 1. FC Köln?
facts.scope: 1973 DFB Cup final after extra time.
facts.evidence: DFB records Borussia’s 2–1 extra-time win. UEFA’s account says Netzer scored the winner after entering in extra time. The DFB Datencenter gives Borussia’s result as 2–1 n.V.

lessons.title: Günter Netzer · Germany’s first Wembley win
lessons.subtitle: Netzer’s performance helped West Germany earn its first victory at Wembley in April 1972.

story.title: A defining international match
story.body: On 29 April 1972, West Germany beat England 3–1 in the European Championship quarter-final. Netzer was the midfield architect.

story.title: A launchpad for a title
story.body: Netzer went on to help Germany defeat Belgium and the Soviet Union at the finals, winning the European title that summer.

facts.label: Wembley match date
facts.prompt: On what date did Günter Netzer help West Germany record its first Wembley win against England?
facts.scope: European Championship quarter-final, England vs West Germany.
facts.evidence: The DFB article identifies 29 April 1972 as the date of the first German Wembley win. DFB dates the 3–1 Wembley win to 29 April 1972.

facts.label: Wembley opponent
facts.prompt: Which national team did Günter Netzer face in West Germany’s first Wembley win on 29 April 1972?
facts.scope: European Championship quarter-final at Wembley, 29 April 1972.
facts.evidence: DFB identifies the landmark match as West Germany’s 3–1 against England. The DFB article names England as the opponent.

facts.label: European title
facts.prompt: Which major national-team title did Günter Netzer help West Germany win in 1972?
facts.evidence: UEFA says Netzer played his part as West Germany beat Belgium and the Soviet Union to lift the trophy. UEFA identifies the tournament victory as the 1972 European Championship.

lessons.title: Günter Netzer · honours and international record
lessons.subtitle: Netzer earned two consecutive German player-of-the-year awards, but his role at the 1974 World Cup was brief.

story.title: Recognised at home
story.body: The DFB lists Netzer as German Footballer of the Year for 1971/72 and 1972/73, and as a two-time Bundesliga champion with Gladbach.

story.title: A brief World Cup role
story.body: Netzer’s only appearance at the 1974 World Cup came in the group match against East Germany. He played for 21 minutes.

facts.label: First player-of-year award
facts.prompt: In which season did Günter Netzer first win Germany’s Footballer of the Year award?
facts.scope: DFB award season, first of Netzer’s two consecutive honors.
facts.evidence: DFB lists his awards in 1971/72 and 1972/73. The DFB profile names 1971/72 as his first award season.

facts.label: 1974 World Cup minutes
facts.prompt: How many minutes did Günter Netzer play in his only appearance at the 1974 FIFA World Cup?
facts.scope: Netzer’s only appearance, West Germany vs East Germany in the 1974 FIFA World Cup group stage.
facts.evidence: DFB says Netzer’s role in the 1974 World Cup was a 21-minute appearance in the group match against the GDR.

facts.label: Senior international caps
facts.prompt: How many senior Germany appearances does the DFB list for Günter Netzer?
facts.scope: Germany senior A internationals in DFB profile.
facts.evidence: The DFB profile lists 37 A-Länderspiele. DFB records 37 senior caps for Netzer.

lessons.title: Lothar Matthäus · first steps in the Bundesliga
lessons.subtitle: Matthäus started his professional career at Gladbach before moving on to Bayern and Inter.

story.title: A young professional
story.body: Matthäus began his professional career in Mönchengladbach in 1979. The DFB records five seasons with Borussia before his first Bayern spell.

story.title: From Germany to Italy
story.body: His next club was Bayern Munich, followed by Inter Milan; he later returned for a second Bayern period and finished in New York.

facts.label: First professional club
facts.prompt: At which club did Lothar Matthäus begin his professional career in 1979?
facts.evidence: DFB says his professional career began in 1979 in Mönchengladbach. The DFB identifies Mönchengladbach as the beginning of his professional career.

facts.label: Gladbach appearances
facts.prompt: How many total matches did the DFB Datencenter list for Lothar Matthäus at Borussia Mönchengladbach?
facts.scope: Borussia club match total, 1 July 1979–30 June 1984.
facts.evidence: The DFB table lists 185 total Borussia matches and separately 162 Bundesliga matches. DFB’s club table lists 185 appearances across competitions.

facts.label: Next club
facts.prompt: Which club did Lothar Matthäus join after Borussia Mönchengladbach in 1984?
facts.scope: Move from Borussia Mönchengladbach in summer 1984.
facts.evidence: The DFB career table dates his Bayern spell from 1 July 1984. DFB lists Bayern as his next club beginning in July 1984.

lessons.title: Lothar Matthäus · the 1990 World Cup opener
lessons.subtitle: Matthäus led Germany’s opening match against Yugoslavia with a goal that became a defining image of the tournament.

story.title: A statement start
story.body: Germany beat Yugoslavia 4–1 in Milan on 10 June 1990. Matthäus scored twice, including the third goal after a long run.

story.title: A personal milestone
story.body: The match was his 75th appearance for Germany. DFB later named his run for the 3–1 goal its Goal of the Year.

facts.label: Opening-match result
facts.prompt: What was the score when West Germany opened the 1990 FIFA World Cup against Yugoslavia?
facts.evidence: DFB’s match record lists Germany’s 4–1 win over Yugoslavia. The DFB match center records the result as 4–1.

facts.label: Matthäus’s goal score
facts.prompt: In West Germany’s 1990 FIFA World Cup opener against Yugoslavia, which score did Lothar Matthäus make with his long-range run and finish?
facts.scope: Matthäus’s second goal in the 1990 World Cup opener.
facts.evidence: The DFB article identifies his run as the 3–1 goal and says it was named Goal of the Year. The DFB article describes his run ending in the 3–1 goal.

facts.label: Appearance milestone
facts.prompt: Which Germany cap number did Lothar Matthäus reach in the 1990 World Cup opener against Yugoslavia?
facts.evidence: DFB says the 4–1 match was Matthäus’s 75th appearance. The DFB account explicitly calls it his number 75 international appearance.

lessons.title: Lothar Matthäus · captaining the 1990 final
lessons.subtitle: In Rome, Matthäus lifted the World Cup as Germany captain after a rematch of the 1986 final.

story.title: A second final against Argentina
story.body: Germany and Argentina met again in the 1990 final. Matthäus captained a side that won 1–0.

story.title: A captain’s moment
story.body: On 8 July, Matthäus became the third DFB captain to raise the World Cup. He later described that moment as extraordinary.

facts.label: World Cup final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Lothar Matthäus captain West Germany to a 1–0 win over Argentina in the 1990 FIFA World Cup final?
facts.evidence: DFB dates the final triumph in Rome to 8 July 1990. The DFB profile names 8 July 1990 as the day he lifted the trophy.

facts.label: Final opponent
facts.prompt: Which team did Lothar Matthäus captain West Germany against in the 1990 FIFA World Cup final?
facts.evidence: DFB describes the final as a repeat meeting with Argentina. DFB states that Germany’s 1990 final was against Argentina.

facts.label: Final score
facts.prompt: What was the score when Lothar Matthäus captained West Germany against Argentina in the 1990 FIFA World Cup final?
facts.evidence: DFB describes Germany’s final win and says Brehme converted the decisive penalty. The final result was 1–0 for Germany over Argentina.

lessons.title: Lothar Matthäus · a record international career
lessons.subtitle: Matthäus combined national records with an exceptional run of individual awards.

story.title: A record holder
story.body: The DFB identifies Matthäus as Germany’s record international, with 150 caps and 75 matches as captain.

story.title: Awards across Europe
story.body: In 1990 he won Germany’s, Europe’s and the world’s top player awards; he defended the world award in 1991.

facts.label: Germany caps
facts.prompt: How many senior international appearances does the DFB list for Lothar Matthäus?
facts.scope: Germany senior internationals, DFB profile as of 2026 article.
facts.evidence: DFB gives his career total as 150 international appearances. The DFB profile identifies 150 caps.

facts.label: Germany captaincies
facts.prompt: How many matches did Lothar Matthäus captain Germany in his international career?
facts.evidence: DFB calls 75 captaincies a DFB record. The article states he was captain exactly 75 times.

facts.label: World player award defense
facts.prompt: In which year did Lothar Matthäus defend the world player-of-the-year award he first won in 1990?
facts.scope: Individual award years during his Inter Milan period.
facts.evidence: DFB says he won the world award in 1990 and defended the title in 1991. The DFB article dates the title defense to 1991.

lessons.title: Augsburg · origins and reunification
lessons.subtitle: The current club’s history reaches back to a 1907 foundation and a later union of city rivals.

story.title: An early beginning
story.body: The club timeline begins with FC Allemania, founded in Augsburg on 8 August 1907. Its first competitive matches came in the Donaugau B-Class.

story.title: A city club takes shape
story.body: After a period of relegation and division, the BCA joined with Schwaben Augsburg’s football department in 1969 and adopted the FC Augsburg name.

facts.label: Foundation date
facts.prompt: On what date was FC Allemania, the club’s earliest named predecessor, founded?
facts.evidence: The club history dates the foundation to 8 August 1907. The official timeline records 8 August 1907.

facts.label: First competitive division
facts.prompt: In which division did FC Augsburg’s predecessor club play its first competitive matches in 1910?
facts.evidence: The official history says its first competitive games were in the Donaugau B-Class. The timeline identifies Donaugau B-Class as the first competitive division.

facts.label: Name after merger
facts.prompt: What name did BC Augsburg adopt after the 1969 football merger with TSV 1847 Schwaben Augsburg?
facts.scope: Club name adopted after the 1969 merger.
facts.evidence: The timeline states BCA renamed to FC Augsburg after the fusion. The official club history says the BCA name changed to FC Augsburg.

lessons.title: Augsburg · the 2011 promotion winner
lessons.subtitle: A late Stephan Hain goal gave Augsburg a 2–1 home win and its first Bundesliga promotion.

story.title: A nervy afternoon
story.body: FSV Frankfurt scored in the third minute on 8 May 2011. Michael Thurk levelled before half-time, leaving Augsburg needing one more goal.

story.title: Hain at the right moment
story.body: Stephan Hain scored in the 85th minute. Augsburg held the lead and secured promotion with a home victory.

facts.label: Promotion-match date
facts.prompt: On what date did FC Augsburg secure its first Bundesliga promotion against FSV Frankfurt?
facts.evidence: The FCA match retrospective dates the promotion win to 8 May 2011. The official match story identifies the date as 8 May 2011.

facts.label: Promotion-match score
facts.prompt: What was the final score in FC Augsburg’s 8 May 2011 home match against FSV Frankfurt that secured promotion to the Bundesliga?
facts.evidence: The match ended 2–1 after Hain’s 85th-minute winner. The official report records a 2–1 home victory.

facts.label: Promotion scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored FC Augsburg’s 85th-minute winner against FSV Frankfurt on 8 May 2011 to secure its first Bundesliga promotion?
facts.evidence: FCA’s match account identifies Hain as the scorer of the winning goal. The report says the corner fell to Hain, who scored in the 85th minute.

lessons.title: Augsburg · a narrow European exit
lessons.subtitle: Augsburg’s first European campaign ended at Anfield after a tight round-of-32 tie with Liverpool.

story.title: A stalemate in Bavaria
story.body: The first leg finished 0–0 in Augsburg. A place in the Europa League round of 16 would be decided in the return match.

story.title: One penalty settles it
story.body: James Milner scored from the spot in the fifth minute at Anfield. Liverpool won 1–0 on the night and on aggregate.

facts.label: Second-leg date
facts.prompt: On what date did Liverpool host FC Augsburg in the 2016 Europa League round-of-32 second leg?
facts.scope: Europa League round-of-32 second leg at Anfield.
facts.evidence: UEFA dates the match to Thursday, 25 February 2016. UEFA’s match report gives the second-leg date as 25 February 2016.

facts.label: Decisive scorer
facts.prompt: Who scored Liverpool’s penalty against FC Augsburg in the 25 February 2016 Europa League second leg at Anfield?
facts.evidence: UEFA says Milner converted the fifth-minute penalty. UEFA identifies James Milner as the penalty scorer.

facts.label: Aggregate score
facts.prompt: What was the aggregate score when Liverpool eliminated FC Augsburg from the 2015/16 Europa League?
facts.evidence: UEFA lists Liverpool’s 1–0 win as the aggregate score after the first leg ended 0–0. The UEFA report states Liverpool 1–0 Augsburg, aggregate 1–0.

lessons.title: Helmut Haller · from Augsburg to Italy
lessons.subtitle: Haller began at BC Augsburg, then became a leading German player in Bologna and Turin.

story.title: Local beginnings
story.body: Born in Augsburg in 1939, Haller joined BC Augsburg at age nine. His first senior goal came away to Offenbacher Kickers in 1957.

story.title: A new football life
story.body: After the 1962 World Cup he moved to Bologna, then transferred to Juventus in 1968 before returning to Augsburg in 1973.

facts.label: Birthplace
facts.prompt: In which city was Helmut Haller born in 1939?
facts.evidence: FCA’s biography states he was born in Augsburg’s Oberhausen district. The official biography gives Augsburg as Haller’s birthplace.

facts.label: Youth club
facts.prompt: At what age did Helmut Haller join BC Augsburg?
facts.scope: Haller’s childhood entry into BC Augsburg.
facts.evidence: The club biography says he joined BC Augsburg at age nine. FCA states that he registered with BC Augsburg at nine.

facts.label: First Italian club
facts.prompt: Which Italian club did Helmut Haller join from BC Augsburg in 1962?
facts.scope: Transfer from BC Augsburg after the 1962 World Cup.
facts.evidence: The FCA biography says he moved from BCA to FC Bologna in 1962. The official article names FC Bologna as the 1962 destination.

lessons.title: Helmut Haller · the opening goal at Wembley
lessons.subtitle: Haller scored first in the 1966 World Cup final, but England won after extra time.

story.title: A fast start
story.body: On 30 July 1966, Haller put West Germany ahead against England in the 12th minute.

story.title: A famous final
story.body: England eventually won 4–2 after extra time. Haller finished the tournament with six goals, second in the scoring list.

facts.label: Final date
facts.prompt: On what date did Helmut Haller score West Germany’s opening goal in the 1966 FIFA World Cup final against England?
facts.scope: World Cup final, England vs West Germany.
facts.evidence: FCA’s biography identifies the final date as 30 July 1966. The official club biography gives 30 July 1966.

facts.label: Opening-goal minute
facts.prompt: In which minute did Helmut Haller score West Germany’s opening goal in the 1966 FIFA World Cup final against England?
facts.evidence: The club report says he scored in the 12th minute. FCA specifies the 12th minute.

facts.label: Final result
facts.prompt: What was the final score after extra time in the 1966 FIFA World Cup final between England and West Germany, in which Helmut Haller scored?
facts.scope: 1966 World Cup final after extra time.
facts.evidence: FCA records the 2–4 defeat after extra time. The biography reports the 2–4 extra-time loss.

lessons.title: Helmut Haller · a durable Scudetto season
lessons.subtitle: Haller played every minute of Bologna’s 1963/64 title season and added a personal award.

story.title: A full campaign
story.body: Bologna and Inter finished level, so the Serie A title went to a deciding match on 7 June 1964. Bologna won 2–0.

story.title: Haller’s contribution
story.body: He played the full 34 league matches and scored seven goals. That year he became the first foreign player named Italy’s Footballer of the Year.

facts.label: League appearances
facts.prompt: How many full Serie A matches did Helmut Haller play for Bologna in the 1963/64 season?
facts.evidence: FCA says Haller played the full 34 matches. The article records all 34 matches played for the full duration.

facts.label: League goals
facts.prompt: How many Serie A goals did Helmut Haller score for Bologna in the 1963/64 season?
facts.evidence: FCA gives his season contribution as seven goals. The official account says he scored seven in the league season.

facts.label: Individual distinction
facts.prompt: Which individual award did Helmut Haller receive in Italy in 1964?
facts.evidence: FCA states he was the first foreigner in Serie A named Italy’s Footballer of the Year in 1964. The club source names his 1964 award as Italy’s Footballer of the Year.

lessons.title: Helmut Haller · the 1974 homecoming
lessons.subtitle: After a decade in Italy, Haller returned to Augsburg and led the side to the Regionalliga Süd title.

story.title: Back in Augsburg
story.body: Haller returned from Juventus in the summer of 1973, becoming the headline signing before the new Regionalliga season.

story.title: A title and a near miss
story.body: He scored ten goals as Augsburg won the 1973/74 Regionalliga Süd. In the promotion round, FCA finished behind Tennis Borussia Berlin.

facts.label: Return year
facts.prompt: In which year did Helmut Haller return from Juventus to his hometown club FC Augsburg?
facts.scope: Haller’s return to his hometown club, summer 1973.
facts.evidence: The FCA account dates his return from Juventus to summer 1973. The club describes his summer 1973 return.

facts.label: Regionalliga goals
facts.prompt: How many Regionalliga Süd goals did Helmut Haller score for FC Augsburg in the 1973/74 season?
facts.evidence: FCA says Haller scored ten goals as he helped lead the team to the title. The 2024 retrospective explicitly gives his tally as ten.

facts.label: Promotion-round rival
facts.prompt: Which club finished ahead of FC Augsburg in the 1974 promotion round after Helmut Haller’s 1973/74 season?
facts.scope: 1974 promotion round after Augsburg won the Regionalliga Süd.
facts.evidence: FCA says Augsburg finished behind Tennis Borussia Berlin. The official history identifies Tennis Borussia Berlin as the team ahead.

lessons.title: Daniel Baier · the long route to Augsburg
lessons.subtitle: Baier moved through Munich and Wolfsburg before building a long career with FC Augsburg.

story.title: Early professional stops
story.body: Baier played for TSV 1860 München from 2003 to 2007, then VfL Wolfsburg. Augsburg first brought him in on loan for 2008/09.

story.title: A permanent home
story.body: After returning briefly to Wolfsburg, Baier joined Augsburg permanently in January 2010 and stayed until 2020.

facts.label: First listed senior club
facts.prompt: Which club did Daniel Baier represent before his 2007 move to VfL Wolfsburg?
facts.scope: Baier’s club career before his first Wolfsburg spell.
facts.evidence: The DFB career table lists TSV 1860 München from July 2003 through June 2007. DFB’s player career record lists TSV 1860 München as his preceding club.

facts.label: Augsburg arrival
facts.prompt: From which club did Daniel Baier initially join FC Augsburg on loan in 2008?
facts.evidence: The FCA says he arrived on loan from Wolfsburg for 2008/09. The official club history names Wolfsburg as the loan club.

facts.label: Permanent signing
facts.prompt: In which month and year did FC Augsburg make Daniel Baier’s move from Wolfsburg permanent?
facts.evidence: FCA says he was permanently signed in January 2010. The club’s farewell account specifies January 2010.

lessons.title: Daniel Baier · an Augsburg debut in the second tier
lessons.subtitle: Baier’s first Augsburg match came in September 2008, before the club’s Bundesliga era.

story.title: A first appearance
story.body: Baier made his FCA debut against SC Freiburg on 14 September 2008 in the second division.

story.title: The result
story.body: Augsburg lost 3–1, but the loan signing’s long relationship with the club had begun.

facts.label: Debut date
facts.prompt: On what date did Daniel Baier make his FC Augsburg debut against SC Freiburg?
facts.evidence: The FCA account gives 14 September 2008 as his debut date. The club’s milestone article dates his FCA debut to 14 September 2008.

facts.label: Debut opponent
facts.prompt: Which club did Daniel Baier’s FC Augsburg debut match on 14 September 2008?
facts.evidence: FCA identifies SC Freiburg as the opponent. The club records his debut against SC Freiburg.

facts.label: Debut score
facts.prompt: What was the score in Daniel Baier’s FC Augsburg debut against SC Freiburg on 14 September 2008?
facts.evidence: The FCA article records a 3–1 defeat to Freiburg. The official account states a 3–1 loss in the second division.

lessons.title: Daniel Baier · a comeback on his 300th appearance
lessons.subtitle: Baier reached two personal milestones during Augsburg’s comeback against Werder Bremen in September 2018.

story.title: Back from two down
story.body: Augsburg trailed Werder Bremen 2–0, then levelled early in the second half. Baier’s milestone match ended in a 3–2 defeat after Davy Klaassen scored in the 75th minute.

story.title: Two round numbers
